writeup.headline: Illumina rates Hold at 62, three points shy of Buy, as strong momentum offsets a high absolute valuation.
writeup.thesis: Illumina scores 62, a Hold, held up by an exceptionally strong trend score of 99: the price is 65.1% above its 200-day average, the shares are up 171.1% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and the price is 1.7% below its 52-week high. Quality (78) and balance sheet (74) are solid, with a 66.4% gross margin, 20.7% FCF margin, diluted share count down 2.5% year on year, and net debt at 0.88 times FCF. Growth scores a middling 54, with TTM revenue growth of 4.9%, though latest-quarter revenue growth of 9.4% year on year shows growth sped up by 4.6 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation is the main drag at 25: in absolute terms the multiples are high, at 9.7x sales, 46.8x FCF and 50.4x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 2.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history, valuation sits near the middle of its own history (EV/EBIT not comparable), with P/S more expensive than at 54 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: After a 171.1% run, a high absolute valuation leaves little room for disappointment.
Q3 2026 results were due after the close on 2026-10-29; a miss or soft guidance could hit the shares.
Several brokers, including Barclays and BofA, still rate the stock Sell, and Stephens downgraded it.
The GRAIL-related securities class action was dismissed, but plaintiffs may amend.
TTM revenue growth of 4.9% is modest for a stock priced at 46.8x FCF.
what_would_change: A 3-point score gain would lift the rating to Buy, for example from stronger growth if quarterly acceleration continues into TTM figures.
A higher valuation score, from a pullback in price or faster FCF and EBIT growth, could also push it over 65.
A drop of 18 points would be needed for Sell, most plausibly from a sharp reversal in the trend score combined with weaker results or guidance.
